newsitem.title: ITALY: ENI reported close to sale of newspaper.
newsitem.headline: ENI reported close to sale of newspaper.

text.p: Energy group ENI is reported to be close to selling its loss-making Milan daily newspaper Il Giorno to an Italian consortium headed by the former Director General of state broadcaster RAI, an Italian newspaper reported Tuesday.
Milan's Il Sole 24 Ore reported that the ENI board was expected to approve the sale of Il Giorno at a meeting sxcheduled for Wednesday to New Day srl, the consortium headed by Gianni Locatelli.

ENI, which has been seeking a buyer for Il Giorno for some time, has poured more than one trillion lire ($650 million) into the venture since it was acquired in the 1950s by the energy group's then chairman Enrico Mattei.
The New Day consortium is 88 percent-owned by publishing company Skira, with 10 percent held by Umberto Seregni, a businessman with printing interests, and 1-2 percent owned by Locatelli himself.
New Day is reported to have offered to pay 25 billion lire to Sogedit, a publishing company owned by ENI, for the paper.
ENI in return has agreed to cover forecast losses of up to 65 billion lire at Il Giorno in 1997 and 1998, Il Sole said.
Poligrafici Editoriale, a Bologna-based publishing group owned by Andrea Riffeser, has lodged a protest with Milan merchant bank Sopaf, which has been advising ENI on the sale of Il Giorno.
Poligrafici, which also bid to acquire Il Giorno, has asked ENI to make public full details of the sale.
